question: Methotrexate for psoriasis is prescribed as a weekly dose, not a daily dose; prescribing it daily instead of weekly is a serious, potentially fatal medication error.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and represents a critical prescribing safety point. MTX for non-oncological indications (psoriasis, RA) is WEEKLY. Daily dosing has caused fatalities. Always explicitly write 'once weekly' and educate the patient.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Methotrexate (MTX) for psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis is always WEEKLY (typically 7.5–25 mg/week). Daily dosing causes fatal bone marrow aplasia and mucositis. This is one of the highest-risk prescribing errors in dermatology — always write the dosing frequency explicitly.
